(1) Johnson (JFQA 2017, read in primary form) computes every straddle return at OptionMetrics closing midpoints on a daily-rebalanced constant-maturity straddle and states in fn 9 that this "overstate[s] returns available to real-time investors"; no cost is netted, and the only investable form (monthly buy-and-hold) keeps just the next-month regression (SLOPE adj. R² 3.8% for 1-month straddles, Table 4 Panel F) while discarding the next-day sorts that give the headline positive low-slope return (+0.44%/day, Table 5 Panel C), which is inside the up-to-100 bp/day closing-quote bias Goyenko-Zhang (2020) document and which Johnson says comes substantially from late 2008. (2) Dew-Becker & Giglio (Chicago Fed WP 2025-17, read) date a break at 2012m5 after which traded-option alphas and ATM-straddle delta-hedged alphas are approximately zero; the hypothesis's 2012-06 to 2026-10 window is entirely post-break. (3) Power: 172 monthly cycles give 28-42 observations per slope quintile; with a monthly SD of 53-57% of premium (Johnson Table 2: 35.7% for the daily-rebalanced version; my free-data proxy: 56.6% for the to-expiry version) the cell SE is 8.5-9.6% of premium, so a positive day-clustered lower bound needs a cell mean of 16.6-18.8% per month (27-31% after Bonferroni over the 80 pre-specified cells); no source reports a long-straddle conditional mean of that size at any date, and daily overlapping entries are only 171 independent windows. (4) A zero-cost proxy screen on the free Cboe VIX9D/VIX3M/VIX6M/VIX/SPX CSVs (2012-06-04 to 2026-09-14, n 3,590 daily / 172 monthly) reproduces the sign of Johnson's effect (low-minus-steep slope +18% of premium [+5, +31] daily, t 2.7; +19% [-6, +44] monthly, t 1.5) but every long-straddle cell is negative in every cut: low-slope -16.5% [-25.1, -7.8] daily, -10.3% [-26.9, +6.3] monthly, -18.3% ex the 2020 crash, -19.9% in 2012-2019, -12.1% in 2020-2026; negative in 13 of 15 years including 2018 (-25%, 97 days) and 2022 (-37%, 84 days), positive only in 2020 (+16%, 61 days); 90.8% of low-slope days have VIX9D above VIX, so the cell buys near-term event/stress premium. The only positive cell is the short straddle in the steepest-slope quintile (+35% of premium gross proxy, ~+20-25% after the VIX-vs-ATM-IV bias, ~+18-23% after costs, lower bound ~0), which is the unconditional VRP carry Dew-Becker & Giglio call beta compensation, is a carry lane under GATE-v2's product-classification gate and registry H15's scope note, and did not pre-empt the 2020 crash (entries 2020-02-10..02-21 were in quintiles 3-4 and lost 4.8-9.6x premium). verdicts.reason: The gross effect is real and well replicated, but the retail proposition fails on the authors' own after-cost table and on power/margin arithmetic. Verified from the primary text (Heston, Jones, Khorram, Li, Mo, JF 78(6) 2023; Sept 2021 and Dec 2021 post-acceptance drafts, Tables 2/4/12/13 identical): quintile momentum lags 2-12 +6.22%/month (t 7.97), lag-1 reversal -4.09% (t -6.18), Sharpe 0.441 monthly / 1.53 annualized, monotone quintiles (-7.77 to -1.55%, all negative), momentum spread present in every option-illiquidity tercile (4.35/5.01/5.07%), rolling five-year averages positive throughout, 282 months 1996-01 to 2019-06, 1,369 straddles/month, OptionMetrics closing mids, held to expiry. Table 13 at the full quoted half-spread (the GATE-v2 marketable-order case): main-sample momentum -6.78% (t -9.63); low-cost (<10% spread) extreme deciles +1.12% (t 0.75), -0.61% (t -0.40) once exercised stock is liquidated; reversal +1.99% (t 1.64); composite +1.98% (t 1.47), -0.30% with exercise costs. Authors' abstract: 'close to zero after paying the full bid-ask spread for options with below-median bid-ask spreads'. New arithmetic: t 0.75 implies a monthly SD of about 25% of notional, so a 95% lower bound > 0 at 1.12%/month needs about 1,357 months (113 years); our window holds about 159 holding months. The paper's SPAN-style margin halves returns (ratio ~2); FINRA 4210 Reg-T for a naked single-name straddle is ~3.5x the straddle value (~70% haircut), and the short leg (the only positive part: low quintile -7.77%/month) is naked single-name straddle writing on 137-274 names a month at the highest approval tier; a 10-name leg carries ~26%/month idiosyncratic noise from an 81%/month single-straddle SD. The long leg alone (the Compass scope) is -1.55%/month gross for the best quintile and about -9 to -10%/month after the C1 10:00 single-name round trip (7-8% of premium), about -24% at the close (11.1% median closing half-spread). Only the top quartile of today's single-name roots meets the paper's <10%-spread eligibility at the close. Replications (Kafer-Morke-Wiest JFQA 2026, 1999-2021 delta-hedged calls, CSM 2-12 +4.57%/yr t 6.98 but HVX alpha 1.27% t 1.82 and 'factor momentum subsumes option momentum'; Wei-Cao-Dong SSRN 4657193 S&P 100 2000-2019 [SEC]; Jones-Khorram-Mo 2020) are all gross results on OptionMetrics closing quotes; no post-2021 out-of-sample, no intraday-quote, no third-party after-cost test exists. Retained only as a bounded ranking filter for which long straddles lose least (<= 3.7% of premium/month vs the universe mean), which cannot make a negative long-straddle cell positive and is moot while no registry result gives Compass a reason to hold single-name straddles.

verdicts.reason: Refuted on the paper's own after-cost table and on what a retail account adds to it. (1) Heston et al. Table 13 (verified from the primary draft): at the "quoted" column — one-way cost = 100 % of the closing quoted half-spread, which is what a marketable order at the NBBO pays under GATE-v2/C1 — momentum is −6.78 %/month (t −9.63) in the main sample and +1.12 % (t 0.75) for the cost-optimised low-spread deciles; reversal +1.99 % (t 1.64); composite +1.98 % (t 1.47); with the stock-liquidation cost after exercise (which retail also pays) −0.61 % (t −0.40), +0.06 % (t 0.05), −0.30 % (t −0.21). The authors: "not profitable if one assumes that the entire quoted spread must be paid." (2) The intermediate "algo/adjusted/effective" columns rest on Muravyev–Pearson (RFS 2020), who state (draft read verbatim) that retail investors cannot time executions and "their costs will equal the conventionally measured effective spreads"; the best retail-claimable column ("effective", 75.8 %, = Hendershott's 2020 EQ 0.74) gives 2.60 % (t 1.75) momentum, 3.46 % (t 2.85) reversal, 3.48 % (t 2.59) composite before margin, 0.88/1.53/1.20 % (t 0.58/1.27/0.87) with exercise costs. (3) New local measurement at the paper's tenor (one-month ATM, closing NBBO, 246 roots, 2023-12→2026-10): median quoted half-spread 11.3 % of mid (p25 5.1, p75 28), only 26 % of roots pass the paper's <10 %-spread filter; a long-short costs 2 × half-spread per month, so at these spreads the main-sample momentum is ≈ −17 %/month and even the liquid tercile's 4.35 % gross is ≈ −2 %/month at the paper's low-cost average (3.06 %/straddle ≈ C1's 10:00 mixed-book 3.5–4.1 %); only ~6 roots are under 2.5 %, too few to form deciles. (4) Short leg = naked single-name straddle writing (Fidelity Level 4, Schwab $25k uncovered-equity minimum); FINRA 4210 margin ratio ≈ 4.1 × premium for the cache-median name vs the paper's SPAN "slightly above 2", so retail margin-adjusted returns are ≈ 24–29 % of gross: +0.3 %/month momentum, +0.5 % reversal, t unchanged. Plus unpriced after-hours exercise (16:00–17:30 ET) and ex-dividend assignment on the short leg. (5) Power: t 0.75 on 282 months implies SD ≈ 25 %/month; a two-sided 95 % lower bound > 0 needs ≈ 1,900 months (momentum), ≈ 400 (reversal), ≈ 500 (composite) at the quoted column and is unreachable with exercise costs; our window is ≈ 159 holding months (2013-07→2026-10), and Tier A legs of 15–30 names raise the long-short SD to ≈ 24 %. (6) The long leg alone — the only Compass-scope expression — is negative in every quintile gross (best −1.55 %) and ≈ −3 to −5 %/month after one entry at intraday liquid-tail spreads, ≈ −13 % at the closing median. Retained only as a zero-cost ranking filter for any long single-name straddle Compass might hold (S13/A5.2), worth ≤ 3.7 % of premium per month gross relative to the universe mean.

The published '3.9%' in the hypothesis could not be verified from any accessible text. (2) The only Compass-scope expression, long-only, is negative in every quintile of every sort (Heston Table 2, 1996-2019: IV-HV low quintile -1.86%/mo, IVOL best -4.74%, term-slope high -2.78%); the long-short is the short leg, which needs the highest approval tier, FINRA 4210 margin (premium + 20% of underlying), retail financing of the delta shares at 5.25% (Robinhood) to 12.075% (Fidelity, <$25k) versus the papers' LIBOR (+0.1 to +0.7 pts/month of drag, the size of the surviving sorts), 5-10 names instead of 79-137 per decile, and American assignment. verdicts.reason: L5 fails all four clauses of the proposition. (1) Not an option edge: the hypothesis itself says "stock-side only"; at C1 half-spreads (3.5-4.1% of premium, single names) a 0.5-delta capture of the long leg's gross 10-25 bp/week (XZZ quintile-1 alpha 10 bp/week; AABC decile-10 1.38%/month) is 5-16 bp of spot against 14-16 bp round trip on a 1-week ATM call, or 28-32 bp plus ~51-62 bp theta on a 30-DTE call held five sessions; execution-costs.md §9 MSFT rows (1.5% half-spread) need 18 bp of move for spread/fees plus 62 bp of theta per five sessions; the debit vertical is worse (two spreads, quarter delta). Negative in every configuration. (2) No lead paper nets out costs: XZZ's full text contains "cost"/"transaction" zero times (counted); CW's abstract is silent; AABC relegate "liquidity frictions" and cost screens to an internet appendix with no net number. Lens default applies. (3) The effect is pre-2012, declining within its own sample (CW abstract: "The degree of predictability decreases over the sample period"; XZZ alpha 40% smaller at a 4-week hold; SKEW weekly autocorrelation 66% falling to ~20%), and later peer-reviewed work places the mechanism in the stock's own closing price pressure (Goncalves-Pinto et al. 2020 abstract: predictability "does not depend on options trading", "stock price pressure being the primary driver"; Muravyev-Pearson-Broussard JFE 2013 abstract: "option price quotes do not contain economically significant information about future stock prices", disagreements resolved by option quotes adjusting) - a one-day reversal that an S07-style screen (signal at close, entry next open, 5-21-session hold) is built to miss. (4) Not testable to the gates: the usable daily window is 2024-01 to 2026-10 (145 weeks / 33 months); scaling the papers' own t-stats, a true effect at FULL published size gives t 1.16 (XZZ raw, 95% lower bound -11 bp/week), 1.55 (XZZ alpha, LB -6), 0.73 (long leg alone, LB -17), 1.43 (AABC raw, LB -0.40%/month); only AABC's dependent double sort (t 5.85 -> 2.4) has any chance, and A5's every-year-sign plus Bonferroni cannot be met. Extending to 2012 needs the stock-EOD lake 2012-2022 (paused), the point-in-time universe (open task), ~220k throttled option-EOD requests (~15 days) or ~1.8M 1-minute chain requests for the 15:45 version the hypothesis specifies. Measured on our own S11 closing-NBBO cache (20,746 root-dates, 471 roots, 2024-2026): the XZZ smirk's median measurement noise is +/-6.3 vol points (OTM-put leg median closing half-spread 19.2%, 45% in the steepest quintile where noise equals the quintile mean of 11 points) against 1.2-3.8-point quintile spacing, and the smirk rank-correlates +0.38 with the put leg's half-spread - at the close the sort is largely a sort on quote width; only 19 of 416 roots have a median put-leg half-spread <= 4%. The engine's r=0.04/q=0 constants manufacture a -2.5 vol-point call-put IV spread in 2012-2016 and a 2.2-point dividend-driven cross-sectional artefact (CW's measure is a put-call-parity quantity; its measured cross-sectional SD is only 4.1 points). What survives is an underpowered stock-side diagnostic outside the options scope.
